subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Mocking and Stubbing
description: A 60-second lesson on Mocking and Stubbing.

hook.text: A test calls a real payment API and charges a customer five dollars every time it runs.

buildup.text: External dependencies make tests slow, expensive, and unpredictable.

discovery.text: Mocks replace real dependencies with controlled fakes that return predictable responses.

twist.text: Over-mocking is dangerous—if you mock everything, you test your mocks, not your code.

climax.text: The team mocks the payment API but keeps the database real. Tests are fast and trustworthy.

punchline.text: Mock what you don't own. Test what you do.

quiz.question: What is the risk of over-mocking?
options: You test your mocks instead of your code
